lessons.title: Where? / There

rules.statement: A. Some of the words used for 'that' are also used for 'there'. B. THERE = DHUWALI/ŊUNHI/ŊUNHA (stationary): verbless Bäya dhuwali/ŋunhi/ŋunha (There's Bäya); with a present-tense verb (person or thing is there NOW) Maṉḏa dhuwali/ŋunhi/ŋunha djäma ga (They are working there); Q Wanha raki'? A Dhuwali/ŋunhi/ŋunha. C. THERE = DHIYALI/ŊUNHILI/ŊUNHALA (stationary, not actually present at this moment — verb not in present tense): Barpuru maṉḏa ga dhiyali/ŋunhili/ŋunhala nhina (user confirmed all three), Gäthura maṉḏa gana dhiyali nhinana, Goḏarr' maṉḏa yurru dhiyali nhini, Galkurru dhiyali! (Wait there); Q Wanha yiki? A Dhiyali ga barpuru ŋorra (It was there yesterday, lit. lying); Q Wanhami/wanhala nhe maḻŋ'maraŋala? (Where did you find it?) A Dhiyali/ŋunhili/ŋunhala; Q Wanhami/wanhala ŋarra yurru nhina? (Where shall I sit?) A Dhiyali. NOTE: suffix -mi, often with infix -ŋu-, may be added (ŋunhilimi/ŋunhiliŋumi), meaning stays the same. D. THERE = DHIPALI/ŊUNHIWILI/ŊUNHAWALA (movement towards): Dhipali/ŋunhiwili/ŋunhawala rulwaŋdhurru! (Put it there!); Q Ŋarra dhu nhäkurru/wanhawala/nhälili gäma? (Where shall I take it?) A Dhipali. NOTE: nhäkurru is not used at Yirrkala. E. THERE = DHIPUŊURU/ŊULIŊURU/ŊULAŊURU/BEŊURU/ŊUNHIŊURU (movement away): Q Wanhaŋuru wandina? (Where did it/he/she run from? — wandina printed, engine waṉḏirri) A Dhipuŋuru/ŋuliŋuru/ŋulaŋuru/beŋuru/ŋunhiŋuru. F. THERE = DHUWALIŊUWUY/ŊUNHIŊUWUY/ŊUNHAŊUWUY (belonging): Q Dhuwala yiki wanhaŋuwuy? (Where does this knife belong / where is it from?) A Dhuwaliŋuwuy/ŋunhiŋuwuy/ŋunhaŋuwuy. NOTES: 1. bala for emphasis (Ŋunha bala maṉḏa ga nhina; Ŋunhawala bala). 2. suffix -dhi/-yi for emphasis: Nhini dhiyalidhi!/dhiyaliyi! 3. the first word of each triple is for the visible and comparatively close; the others also serve when the person or thing is not seen.

lessons.title: This and that with possessive adjectives

rules.statement: When 'this' or 'that' qualify a possessive adjective, the demonstrative takes the SAME form as the possessor, not the head. A. Possessive Adjective (1), -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu (Lessons 13, 35): Ŋatha ŋayi djaw'yurruna dhiyaku yothuwa (He took this child's food); dhiyaki/ŋuruki/ŋuruku yothuwa (that child's). B. Possessive Adjective (2), -gala/-kala/-wala (Lesson 36): 1-2 Dhiyakala/Ŋurikala/Ŋurukala miyalkkala waṯuy yothunha ḻawuŋala (This/That woman's dog bit the baby); 3-4 Dhiyakala miyalkkala bathilili galkara ŋayi (He put it into this woman's dilly bag); 5-6 Ŋayi gana ŋorrana dhiyakala/ŋurikala/ŋurukala yolŋuwala bala'ŋura (He was sleeping in this/that man's house); 7-8 Walala marrtjina dhiyakala yolŋuwala ṉakuy (They went in this man's canoe). C. Possessive Adjective (3), infix -galaŋu-/-kalaŋu-/-walaŋu- (Lessons 51-52) — the demonstrative takes the same infixed form: 1-2 Dhiyakalaŋuwa/Ŋurikalaŋuwa/Ŋurukalaŋuwa yolŋuwalaŋuwa miyalkku ŋayi ga djälthirri (He wants this/that man's wife); 3-4 Djäka/Djäga dhiyakalaŋuwa yolŋuwalaŋuwa ŋathawa (Look after this man's food); 5-6 Gurrupulu dhiyakalaŋuwala yolŋuwalaŋuwala miyalkkala (Give it to this man's wife); 7-8 Dhiyakalaŋuwuŋu yolŋuwalaŋuwuŋu miyalkkuŋu ŋarra dhäwu märraŋala (I got the story from this man's wife); 9-10 Dhiyakalaŋuwuy yolŋuwalaŋuwuy miyalkkalaŋuwuy ŋarra dhäwu märraŋala (I heard a tale about this man's wife); 11-12 Dhiyakalaŋuŋuru miyalkkalaŋuŋuru bathiŋuru ŋayi manaŋina (He stole it from this woman's dillybag). NOTE after 8: suffixes may be shortened (dhiyakala yolŋuwala miyalkkuŋu). NOTES: 1. these long words may be avoided by framing the sentence differently, but are used when necessary. 2. word order is not fixed.

lessons.title: Now / Then

rules.statement: A. Some of the words for 'this' and 'here' are also used for 'now' (cf. Lessons 54, 55): Dhuwala bala ŋarra dhu marrtji / Dhiyaŋu bala ŋarra dhu marrtji (I'll go now — dhiyaŋu bala lit. 'on this (day)'); Dhuwala nhuŋu ŋatha dhiyaku bala (This is your food for now); Dhipuŋuru bala ga yäna bili ga Bäpa yurru buna... (From now until Bäpa comes...). NOTE: the phrase 'ga yäna bili ga / until' will be dealt with in a later Lesson. B. Some of the words for 'that' and 'there' are also used for 'then' (cf. Lessons 56, 57): Ga ŋunhi(yi)/ŋuliŋuru(yi)/ŋunhiŋuru(yi)/beŋuru(yi) walala marrtjina (And then they went).

lessons.title: (a) Present continuous negative (b) Yesterday past negative

rules.statement: A. The present continuous (Lesson 10) uses ga with the PRIMARY form: Walala buḻ'yun ga. B. When made NEGATIVE the verb changes to the SECONDARY form and ga becomes gi (ga is primary, gi is secondary): Walala gi yaka buḻ'yurru (They are not playing). MORE EXAMPLES (negator fronted): Bäyŋu walala gi ḻuki / ŋorri / gori / ḻupthurru / djäma / wukirri (They are not eating / sleeping / ashamed (shy) / washing / working / writing).

C. The yesterday past (Lesson 17) uses the PRIMARY form: Barpuru ŋayi nhäma; continuous adds ga (Lesson 18): Barpuru ŋayi nhäma ga. D. When made NEGATIVE it changes to the SECONDARY form: Barpuru ŋayi yaka nhäŋu (He didn't see (it) yesterday); Maṉḏa barpuru yaka ḻuki / ŋorri / ḻupthurru (They didn't eat / sleep / wash yesterday). Continuous aspect (Lesson 18): Yaka ŋarra gi buḻ'yurru / ŋorri / djäma (I didn't play/wasn't playing; sleep; work). NOTE: yesterday past continuous negative is the same as present continuous negative — context, or an adverb of time (yesterday, now), makes clear which is meant. E. Often the QUATERNARY form is used with the negative (yaka/bäyŋu) for an event of 'yesterday' or the recent past (compare Lesson 41): Barpuru ŋayi yaka nhänha(ra) / monha(ra) / ŋänha(ra) / ḻupthuna(ra) (didn't see / forget / hear / wash yesterday). NOTES: 1. at Elcho the PRIMARY form is sometimes used with yaka/bäyŋu (Barpuru ŋarra yaka nhäma; Walala ga yaka buḻ'yun; Walala gana yaka buny'tjurruna) — attributed to Dhaŋu'mirri people (Wangurri, Gälpu) speaking weak Gupapuyŋu. 2. at Yirrkala these negative forms are not thoroughly investigated, but quaternary+negative is recorded for 'yesterday': Yawungu ŋarra ŋanya yaka nhänhara (yawungu is more common at Yirrkala than barpuru; also used at Milingimbi and Elcho). 3. ga/gi as continuous aspect are not used at Yirrkala.

notes: Mechanism: the two generator gates that returned null (present-continuous negative since Lesson 10; pasado_ayer negative flagged 'not yet taught' since Lesson 41) are replaced by Lesson 60 builds — negative present continuous: [sujeto, gi, yaka, II] with bäyŋu, the fronted Bäyŋu/Yaka orders (the book's MORE EXAMPLES shape) and the Elcho primary+ga+yaka form (note 1) as alternatives; negative yesterday past: [barpuru, sujeto, yaka, II] with bäyŋu, the E quaternary IV and IV+ra, the Elcho primary, and barpuru→yawungu (note 2) as alternatives; negative yesterday continuous: [sujeto, gi, yaka, II] (same construction as present, per the NOTE), fronted Yaka giving the book's exact 'Yaka ŋarra gi buḻ'yurru'

Analyzer: EN is/are/am + not + gerund (pronoun path, nominal-subject path, and the not-ashamed participle) and ES no + estar-present + gerundio (pronoun path, subject-dropped path, and the leading-no branch) now produce tiempo continuo + polaridad negativa; the was/were-not and no+estaba paths from Lesson 41 already produced the pasado_ayer IR — only the generator was blocking

lessons.title: Let's / About to

rules.statement: A. 'Let's' is inclusive, so ŋali (two people) or (ŋi)limurru (more than two) is used with the PRIMARY verb form and no verb particle; suffix -na may be added or omitted, same meaning: Ŋali marrtji(na) / ŋorra(na) / roŋiyirri(na) / bathan(na) / nhina(na) / guŋga'yun(na) (Let's go / lie down / go back / cook (it) / sit / help); (Ŋi)limurru ḻupthun(na) / buḻ'yun(na) / ḏar'ṯaryun(na) / ḻiyaman(na) / ḻithan(na) / buny'tjun(na) (Let's have a wash / play / sing / sing / get dry-warm / smoke). B. The bare primary with ŋarra (I) means 'I'm about to / going to': Ŋarra roŋiyirri(na) / buḻ'yun(na) / ḻupthun(na) / marrtji(na) / buny'tjun(na). Said with a questioning tone it means 'Do you mind if...?' / 'Shall I...?': Ŋarra buny'tjun(na)? NOTE: the same-day future (Lesson 11) with ŋarra/ŋali/ŋilimurru also indicates being about to: Ŋarra yurru ḻupthun(na); Ŋali yurru ḻupthun(na); Ŋilimurru yurru ḻupthun(na).

(rendered as the declarative plus '?'); ES triggers: the nosotros subjunctive hortative (comamos, juguemos, cantemos, fumemos — subjuntivoNosotros derives -emos→-ar with gu/qu/c reversions and -amos→-er/-ir with diphthong reversions; previously these were wrongly read as 2sg imperatives) and 'estoy a punto de + infinitivo'

lessons.title: Habitual aspect: ŋuli

rules.statement: A. The verb particle ŋuli marks habitual occurrence (every day/always/often/sometimes). B. HABITUAL PRESENT = primary + ŋuli (ga): Djämalili ŋayi ŋuli (ga) marrtji (yäna) bitjan bili (He goes to work every day); Ŋarali' ŋayi ŋuli (ga) buny'tjun (yäna) bitjan bili (He smokes all the time/every day); Ŋatha ŋayi ŋuli (ga) ḻuka (yäna) bitjan bili (He eats food all the time); Dharrwamirri ŋayi ŋuli gurrukama (ga) / ḻupthun (ga) / buḻ'yun (ga) (He often wears (it) / washes / plays). NOTES: 1. primary changes to SECONDARY if negative: Ŋayi ŋuli (gi) bäyŋu ŋatha ḻuki (He doesn't eat any food). 2. sometimes the present continuous alone is used: Ŋayi ga ŋatha ḻuka yäna bitjan bili. C. HABITUAL PAST = quaternary + ŋuli (ganha): Ŋäthili ŋayi ŋuli (ganha) miyapunu ḻukanha(ra) (He used to eat turtle before); dhäwu djawarrkthuna(ra) (preach); schoollili marrtjinya(ra) (go to school); ŋarali' buny'tjuna(ra) (smoke). NOTES: 1. the continuous aspect (ga/gi/ganha) may be omitted. 2. ga/gi/ganha are not used at Yirrkala. 3. yäna is a word often used, with no real English equivalent; it may be omitted. 4. in Gupapuyŋu ŋuli is often abbreviated to li (Ŋayi li ga marrtji schoollili) — not in Yirrkala dialects. 5. ŋuli doesn't always mean habitual action; sometimes it means 'that time' (nhe ŋarranha gurrupan ŋuli — you gave me that time).

lessons.title: Might / Should / Would / Must

rules.statement: A. MIGHT (future), three constructions: (1) balaŋu + SECONDARY: Ŋayi balaŋu djaw'yurru / rirrikthurru / bakthurru / dhiŋguŋu / bakmaraŋu (He might take (it) / get sick / get hurt-it might break / she might die / break it); (2) bäna balaŋu + secondary: Ŋayi bäna balaŋu djaw'yurru...; (3) balaŋu yurru/dhu + PRIMARY: Ŋayi balaŋu yurru/dhu djaw'yun / rirrikthun / bakthun / dhiŋgama / bakmarama. NOTE 1: the continuous secondary gi is sometimes used (Ŋayi balaŋu gi bäna yaka ŋayathulu djurra' — I'd better take a book, she might not have one); gi not at Yirrkala. NOTE 2: MIGHT HAVE (past) = bäna balaŋu + QUATERNARY: Ŋayi bäna balaŋu djaw'yuna(ra) (He might have taken them); Ŋayi bäna balaŋu Gattjilili marrtjinya(ra) (He might have gone to Gattji); nhe bäna balaŋu bakthuna(ra) (You might have got hurt); with Dhä-birrka'yurru Wäwanha (Ask Wäwa) and Yaka ŋarra marŋgi (I don't know) as dialogue frames.

B. SHOULD/WOULD (future), three constructions: (1) balaŋu + secondary: Nhe (gi) balaŋu guŋga'yurru ŋanya (You should help him) / wutthurru / marŋgikuŋu; (2) ŋuli + secondary: Nhe ŋuli (gi) ŋanya guŋga'yurru; (3) balaŋu ŋuli + secondary: Nhe balaŋu ŋuli ŋanya guŋga'yurru. NOTES: gi often used with ŋuli and balaŋu, not essential; not at Yirrkala. SHOULD/WOULD HAVE (past) = balaŋu + QUATERNARY: Balaŋu walala ḏiltjilili marrtjinya(ra) (They should have gone to the bush); Balaŋu walala guya barrtjuna(ra) (speared some fish); nhuna waŋanha(ra) (spoken to you); ŋatha bathana(ra) (cooked some food); Ŋapurru balaŋu marrtjinya(ra), ŋanydja... (We would have gone, but...) / märranha(ra) / roŋiyinya(ra) / ŋäŋ'thuna(ra). NOTES: context and intonation say whether 'should have' or 'would have'; ganha sometimes used, not at Yirrkala. C. MUST: same forms as should — Nhe ŋuli (gi) yaka ŋanya waŋi (You must not talk to him); more forceful with the future: Nhe yurru yaka ŋanya waŋa.

lessons.title: (a) English adjective = Gupapuyŋu verb (b) Present tense - tertiary form (c) Have

rules.statement: A. Often an English adjective is a verb in Gupapuyŋu: barrarirri/be afraid, djulŋithirri/be happy, mukthun/be quiet, djawaryun/be tired, rirrikthun/be sick, gurku'yun/be ready, ŋar'ŋaryun/be thirsty, gora/be shy-ashamed, wuyun/be sorry (for someone). B. The TERTIARY form describes how one feels where English uses the present: Ŋarra (dhuwala) barrarina / djulŋithina / djawaryurruna / rirrikthurruna / gurku'yurruna / ŋar'ŋaryurruna / gorana (I am afraid / happy / tired / sick / ready / thirsty / ashamed). C. Gupapuyŋu adjectives are often verbalised: djaŋŋarr/hungry → Ŋarra (dhuwala) djaŋŋarrthina; guyiŋarr/cold → guyiŋarryina; gorrmur/hot → gorrmurthina; maḏakarritj/angry → maḏakarritjthina; djäl/desirous → djälthina. NOTES: 1. the tertiary means 'have become' (Ŋarra barrarina — I have become afraid). 2. where English uses 'have' with a verb the tertiary is frequent: Ŋapurru (dhuwala) marrtjina dhipala (We have come here). 3. the PRIMARY form can also describe how one feels: Ŋarra ga rirrikthun. 4. dhuwala is optional but very common, no English equivalent (see Lesson 65). 5. the tertiary-for-present also occurs beyond feelings (religious example omitted by request; sometimes ga + primary instead, but tertiary seems more common).

notes: FraseIR.sentimiento: PRON + SER + feeling-word → the verb's TERTIARY (tiempo pasado_hoy confirmado) with two options everywhere: pron→'pron dhuwala' (notes 4 and Lesson 65) and tertiary→'ga + primary' (note 3); PARTICIPIOS_ESTATIVOS_EN widened (happy/tired/sick/ill/ready/thirsty/sorry → the new 'be X' verb entries over djulŋithirri/djawaryun/rirrikthun/gurku'yun/ŋar'ŋaryun/wuyun), and adjectives flagged sentimiento (hungry djaŋŋarr, cold guyiŋarr, hot gorrmur', angry maḏakarritj) verbalise through the Lesson 49 derivation

HAVE + participle (note 2): PRON + have/has + PARTICIPLE → tertiary (i have eaten → Ŋarra ḻukana; we have come here → Ŋilimurru marrtjina räli dhipala); ES: haber (he/has/ha/hemos/han) + participio (-ado/-ido reversed to the infinitive), estar + participle map (cansado/enfermo/preparado/contento/sediento...), and the tener idioms (tengo hambre/frío/calor/sed → djaŋŋarrthina/guyiŋarryina/gorrmur'thina/ŋar'ŋaryurruna)

Multi-token exact verb forms now compose as ga-present (we have a wash → Ŋilimurru ga ḻupthun; me duele la cabeza → Ŋarra ga ḻiya rathala'yun) — guarded against past readings (put) and ES imperatives (ponte de pie); TRAP HIT AGAIN: a second 'have a headache' vocab entry (L38, lema rathala'yun without ḻiya) already existed and silently won — merged into one entry with lema ḻiya-rathala'yun (the book prints ḻiya rathala'yun in Lessons 65-66)

lessons.title: Special uses of dhuwala / ŋunhi / dhuwali

rules.statement: A. dhuwala ('here', Lessons 55/57) and ŋunhi/dhuwali ('there') are often used where English says nothing — no real equivalent: Ŋarra dhuwala ḻiya rathala'yurruna (I (here) have a headache); Nhe dhuwala marŋgi manymakku romgu (You (here) know the good way); Linyu dhuwala marrtjina nhänharawa nhuŋu (We (here) have come to see you); (religious example omitted by request — its frame, [pronoun] dhuwala [verb-III] dhipala [purpose-nominal], is the same as the previous example); Ŋayi dhuwala mirithirri manymak (He (here) is very good). NOTE: with dhuwala the person referred to is the speaker or someone close. Nhuma dhuwali yätjkurru mirithirri (You (there) are very naughty); Walala ŋunhi ḻukthurruna storelili (They (there) gathered at the store); Ŋayi ŋunhi manymak yolŋu (He (there) is a good person); Ŋarra ŋunhi barpuru rirrikthun ga (I (there) was sick yesterday). NOTE 1: dhuwali when the person can be seen; ŋunhi with speaker usually takes a past verb.

notes: Implemented as the discourse substitution the Lesson 64 sentimiento/have frames already carry: pron → 'pron dhuwala' with the nota naming dhuwali (visible) and ŋunhi (not seen) — Ŋarra dhuwala ḻiya rathala'yurruna composes as the alternative of 'i had a headache' and Ŋilimurru dhuwala marrtjina räli dhipala of 'we have come here'

The remaining examples (marŋgi with dhuwala, mirithirri 'very', yätjkurru 'naughty', ḻukthun 'gather', storelili) are attested; extending the discourse particle to verbless and estado clauses, and composing mirithirri for 'very' (the engine strips GRADOS), stay pending

lessons.title: Adverbial expression (8a) cause: -dhu/-thu/-yu/-y and -gala/-kala/-wala

rules.statement: A. Another use of -dhu/-thu/-yu/-y is CAUSE. B. On a thing/noun (form rules: Lesson 22): Ŋarra (dhuwala) djawaryurruna gorrmur'yu / guyiŋarryu / rirrakayyu / watay / djämay yindiy (I am tired because of the heat / cold / noise / wind / hard work); NOTE: gorrmur and guyiŋarr are nouns as well as adjectives. Ŋayi ga rirrikthun miḻŋiny'thu (diarrhoea) / ŋalparr'yu (a cold) / ḏoguy-ḏowuy (the waves) / guyay ḏulkiy (eating a bad fish); NOTE: the adjective (ḏulki) takes the same suffix as its noun. C. The same suffix (-y after a vowel) on the LONG QUATERNARY verb: Ŋarra ga djawaryun nhinanharay / marrtjinyaray / waṉḏinyaray / buḻ'yunaray / dhärranharay weyindhu (tired from sitting / walking / running / playing / standing a long while); NOTE: the adverb weyin takes the same suffix. Ŋayi ga rirrikthun guyaŋanharay (worrying) / gapuy monukthu ḻukanharay (drinking salt water). D. -gala/-kala/-wala on a PERSON denotes cause (form rules: Lesson 26): Ŋarra ga gora wäwawala / gäthuwala / nhumalaŋgala / walalaŋgala (ashamed because of my brother / son / you-plural / them); Ŋarra ga ḻiya rathala'yun djamarrkuḻi'wala yatjunaray (headache because of the children yelling) / yawirriny'kala buḻ'yunaray / yolŋuwala giritjinyaray / nhokala waŋanharay. E. QUESTIONS: Nhaliy nhe burakina? (How did you get hurt, lit. with what) — Buthuluy (on a bottle), Djambakay (a piece of tin), Garay (a spear), Maranydjalkthu (a stingray). NOTES: 1. -yu at Yirrkala instead of -y. 2. burakirri = get hurt pierced (spear, stingray); bakthun = get hurt by falling/bumping. 3. word order not fixed.

examples.en: I am tired because of the heat
I am tired because of the cold
I am tired because of the noise
I am tired because of the wind
He is sick because of a head cold
I am tired because of sitting
I am tired because of playing
I am ashamed because of my brother

notes: Composed by REUSING the instrument/comitative machinery, exactly as the book frames it ('another use of suffix -dhu...', 'see Lesson 22/26'): the wrapper rewrites 'because of' → 'with' (or 'by' before a gerund, feeding the Lesson 46 verbal instrument) and ES 'a causa de(l)' / 'por culpa de(l)' → 'con'; thing-causes take sufijoAgente (gorrmur'yu, watay, ŋalparr'yu), verbal causes the long quaternary + -y (nhinanharay, buḻ'yunaray), person-causes the comitative -gala/-kala/-wala (wäwawala); the sentimiento clauses accept the cause because hayVerboAccion now recognizes the feel-participles and multi-token verb phrases

New nouns: heat gorrmur', noise rirrakay, wind wata, bottle buthulu, stingray maranydjalk, head cold ŋalparr'; burakirri entered as 'be pierced' (note 2 — the nhaliy question keeps bakthun for 'get hurt', burakina attested)

Attested, not composed: djämay yindiy (hard work), miḻŋiny'thu, ḏoguy/ḏowuy (waves), guyay ḏulkiy (adjective agreement on the cause exists in the instrument renderer, but 'eating a bad fish' arrives as a gerund phrase), weyindhu agreement, and the D person+verb pairs (djamarrkuḻi'wala yatjunaray family — person-cause plus verbal-cause in one clause); the bare-instrument answer fragments (Buthuluy, Garay...) pending as fragments
ES bare 'por' deliberately keeps the Lesson 31 purpose reading — only 'a causa de(l)' / 'por culpa de(l)' are cause

lessons.title: Adverbial expression (8b) cause suffix: -buy/-puy/-wuy

rules.statement: A. -buy/-puy/-wuy also denotes CAUSE (cf. Lesson 66). Added to: 1a things (rules Lesson 39), 1b persons (infix -galaŋu- + -wuy), 2 the SHORT quaternary verb (Yirrkala probably the long form). B. Miyalk dhiŋgaŋala ragalkpuy / rerripuy / bunhapuy / galkirrinyawuy / guyapuy ḻukanhawuy (The girl died because of sorcery / sickness / being beaten / falling / eating the fish). C. Ŋayi dhu nhuna dhägir'yun bindharr'yunawuy / manaŋinyawuy / djämapuy yätjanhawuy / miyalkkalaŋuwuy bunhapuy / marramba'puy (He'll punish you for swearing / stealing / doing it badly / beating the woman / adultery). D. (jealous-of frame; religious example omitted by request: [name]nha mel-dhi'yurruna ... rur'maranhawuy / walŋakunhawuy). E. Ŋarra ŋar'ŋaryurruna waṉḏinyawuy / ŋunhiŋuwuy marrtjinyawuy / waŋanhawuy weyinbuy (I was thirsty because of running / that walk / talking for a long time). F. Ŋarra ŋanya buku-gurrpara djäkapuy yothuwalaŋuwuy / nhokalaŋuwuy / maṉḏaŋgalaŋuwuy (I thanked her for looking after the baby / you / them). G. -guŋu/-kuŋu/-wuŋu marks the PERSON WHO DID the action: Yothu ga ŋäthi wutthunawuy ŋäṉḏi'mirriŋuwuŋu / Wandjukkuŋu / nhanukuŋu / ŋarrakuŋu (The child is crying because of being smacked by its mother / Wandjuk / him / me). H. Q Nhäpuy ŋayi dhiŋgaŋala? (What did he die of?) A Miḻŋiny'puy / Rerripuy / Bunhawuy. NOTES: 1. Yirrkala: long quaternary; rawalk for ragalk; dhäḏir'yun for dhägir'yun. 2. word order not fixed. COMPARISON 66/67: either suffix often works; -dhu is right when the cause means 'by means of/through'; when 'for' can replace 'because', ONLY -buy/-puy/-wuy (punish for swearing, jealous because of healing).

examples.en: The girl died because of being beaten
The girl died because of falling
He will punish you for swearing
He will punish you for stealing
He will punish you for adultery
I was thirsty because of running
I thanked her for looking after the baby

notes: Composed by extending the pertenencia (-puy) machinery: VerboVocabulario.causaBuy (dhägir'yun, buku-gurrpan, dhiŋgama, ŋäthi, ŋar'ŋaryun) opens extraerPertenencia's gate (previously tell-verbs only) and lets of/de accept plain-noun causes (rerripuy); the wrapper rewrites 'because of' → 'about' (and 'for'/'por' → 'about'/'sobre' — for punish always, for the others only before a gerund/infinitive, keeping Lesson 31's crying-for-milk -wa and thank-you-for-food intact); 'being + participle' resolves through the participle table (being beaten → buma → bunhawuy); gerunds now match multi-token verbs (looking after → djäka)

The renders are Lesson 39/46 forms untouched: noun cause -puy at clause end, verb cause = short quaternary + wuy (+puy and long -ra + Yirrkala options), person cause = infix -kalaŋuwuy; engine orders the F person before the verb-nominal (book djäkapuy first, order free, note 2)
Nhäpuy question: EN what+did+PRON+V+of and ES ¿de qué + pretérito (persona from the conjugation, 1sg read as 3sg) through the generic question block (Nhäpuy ŋayi dhiŋgaŋala? letter-exact)

Attested, not composed: C-3 djämapuy yätjanhawuy (doing it badly), C-4 miyalkkalaŋuwuy bunhapuy (person-object inside the verbal cause), E-2 ŋunhiŋuwuy marrtjinyawuy (demonstrative cause), E-3 weyinbuy agreement, all of G (-guŋu agent of the cause — PertenenciaIR has no agent fields), the H answer fragments, and D (religious, omitted); ES F 'le agradecí por cuidar al bebé' still null (clitic-infinitive object chain)

New vocab: swear bindharr'yun, sorcery ragalk (rawalk basesAlternas), adultery marramba', diarrhoea miḻŋiny'; smack on wutthun; bunhapuy printed in B-3 but Bunhawuy in H-3 (engine composes bunhawuy, -puy as option)

lessons.title: Derived words (12): verb + -buy/-puy/-wuy = adjective

rules.statement: A-C. -buy/-puy/-wuy on the SHORT quaternary makes an ADJECTIVE meaning 'as a result of / caused by' (the same form Lesson 67 called an adverbial of cause — here it modifies a noun). D. gothan/cook-boil → mapu' gothanawuy (a cooked egg); manaŋirri/steal → rrupiya manaŋinyawuy (stolen money); ŋämin/paint (gr. 6) → bala' ŋäminawuy; dharrpan/hide → girri' dharrpanawuy; dhaḻ'yun/shut → dhurrwara dhaḻ'yunawuy; ḻumbakthun/bend → gara ḻumbakthunawuy; dhiŋgama/die → weṯi dhiŋganhawuy (a dead wallaby); guyaŋa/think → dhäwu guyaŋanhawuy (a thought-up story); barr'yun/split → guṉḏa barr'yunawuy; bakthun/break → yiki bakthunawuy; wunya'yun/get lost → yothu wunya'yunawuy; garrpin/bandage → ḻuku garrpinawuy. NOTE: dead can also be rakuny, cooked also borum, broken also bakpak. E. Sometimes no English adjective exists: yolŋu dharpunhawuy (a man who has been speared), yolŋu dhägir'yunawuy (a person being punished), rupa ŋurrkanhawuy (a thrown-away tin), dharpa mälakmaranhawuy (crossed wood). F. Meaning depends on transitivity: intransitive = the noun did it (yothu ḻupthunawuy — a child who washed himself; guṉḏa barr'yunawuy — split of its own accord); transitive = done to the noun (yothu ḻupmaranhawuy — washed by someone; guṉḏa barr'maranhawuy — split by someone).

notes: Mechanism: adjetivoResultado — an EN participle (via the participle/past tables) or ES participio (-ado/-ido + irregulars roto/muerto/abierto...) that resolves to a verb synthesizes the adjective clave 'resultado:<verbo>' with gup = short quaternary + wuy (puy as base alterna); wired into palabraDeTipo and adjetivoDeTokens (so every NP position takes it) and resolved generator-side in buscarPalabra like the agente: nouns

The pure adjectives WIN where they exist, exactly as the book's note says: cooked → borum, broken → bakpak, dead → rakuny (the derived gothanawuy/bakthunawuy/dhiŋganhawuy stay attested); engine shut = gungama → gunganhawuy (book dhaḻ'yunawuy — different verb, same derivation) and lost → moma → monhawuy (book wunya'yunawuy); ES symmetric (dinero robado, huevo cocido via cocer→gothan, cuchillo roto)

E and F (dharpunhawuy, dhägir'yunawuy, ŋurrkanhawuy, ḻupmaranhawuy, barr'maranhawuy transitive pairs) attested — the intransitive/transitive contrast is data the derivation already respects (the clave picks the verb actually named); mälakmaranhawuy left attested
New verbs: ŋämin paint, ḻumbakthun bend, barr'yun split, garrpin bandage, gothan boil (es cocer); guṉḏa printed with ṉ (user confirmed; gunḏa at L25 — interchangeable)

lessons.title: Adjectival expression: verb and thing + -buy/-puy/-wuy, person + -guŋu/-kuŋu/-wuŋu

rules.statement: A-B. Enlarging the Lesson 68 adjective. C. -buy/-puy/-wuy is also added to the THING with which the action is done: bala' djuḏum'puy ŋäminawuy (a mud-plastered house), yolŋu djimaṉḏi'puy dharpunhawuy (a person speared with a fish-spear), miyapunu guṉḏirrpuy gothanawuy (a turtle roasted in ant-bed). D. -guŋu/-kuŋu/-wuŋu is added to the person BY WHOM the action is done: rrupiya manaŋinyawuy djamarrkuḻi'wuŋu (money stolen by the children), yolŋu dharpunawuy Djäwawuŋu, dhäwu guyaŋanhawuy miyalkkuŋu, yiki gurrupanawuy Raymanguŋu, miyapunu guṉḏirrpuy gothanawuy Stephenguŋu, weṯi märriyaŋbuy wutthunawuy Wandjukkuŋu, bala' djuḏum'puy ŋäminawuy ŋarrakuŋu. NOTE: the English passive can sometimes be translated this way (religious example omitted by request), but only when the phrase still DESCRIBES the noun now. E. -buy/-puy/-wuy also describes the OBJECT of a verb in the act of doing something: Ŋarra nhäŋala miyalknha ŋupanawuy / marrtjinyawuy / ŋäthinyawuy / waṉḏinyawuy / buḻ'yunawuy / ŋorranhawuy (I saw a girl (in the act of) following / walking / crying / running / playing / lying down); Ŋarra ŋäkula ŋanya waŋanhawuy / ḻiyamanawuy / ŋäthinyawuy (I heard him talking / singing / crying).

notes: E composed: ObjetoIR.enActo — an object NP ending in a gerund (EN and ES 'vi a una niña corriendo') keeps the head and renders the verb's short quaternary + wuy after the clause, with the bare -ra form (Lesson 71-D) and the Yirrkala long form as options

C (instrument inside the adjectival phrase) is attested, not composed; D (the -guŋu agent) now composes in the verbless frame: an EN 'by'-phrase on a resultado: adjective predicate carries through as comitativo and renders formaGunu after the adjective (Dhuwala bala' ŋäminawuy Wandjukkuŋu) — the same suffix machinery as Lesson 30; ES 'por'-passives and the verbal-clause -guŋu agent (Lesson 67-G) remain pending; the passive NOTE's semantic restriction is recorded

Book prints ŋorranhawuy for lying down and ŋupanawuy for following (engine following = malthun/ŋupan both exist); ES side renders the Lesson 66 -ray instrument reading for 'corriendo' when the frame is read as cause — both prints in the book

lessons.title: Derived words (13): verb + -buy/-puy/-wuy = noun

rules.statement: B. The same short-quaternary + -buy/-puy/-wuy construction produces a NOUN: dhägir'yunawuy punishment, mata'maranhawuy prisoner, wukirriwuy writing, bokmanawuy creation, ḻiyamirriyanhawuy prayer, guyaŋanhawuy thoughts, nyäl'yunawuy lie(s), märr-ŋamathinyawuy love, bindharr'yunawuy swearing, ḻiya-ḻupmaranhawuy baptized one, wäwungunhawuy promised one, märr-djulkthunawuy unbelief, märr-yuwalkthinyawuy belief-faith, marŋgikunhawuy teachings. C. -guŋu/-kuŋu/-wuŋu marks the PERSON who performed the action: ŋarrakuŋu wukirriwuy (my writing), limurruŋguŋu ḻiyamirriyanhawuy (our prayers); (religious examples omitted by request).

notes: sustantivoDeVerbo: an explicit deverbal-noun table (punishment/thoughts/prayer(s)/teaching(s)/writing(s)/swearing/lies/creation/belief/faith/unbelief; ES castigo/pensamientos/escritura/mentiras/creencia/fe/creación) resolves to the verb and synthesizes clave 'accion:<verbo>' with gup = short quaternary + wuy (bare -ra as base alterna, Lesson 71-C), resolved generator-side in buscarPalabra; the table is deliberately closed — a bare-gerund route would steal the Lesson 46 verbal origins/instruments

ORDER TRAPS: the deverbal lookup must run BEFORE nombreAgentivo ('prayer' was becoming the agent noun ḻiyamirriyanhamirri 'one who prays'), and extraerPertenencia's about-branch must try the VERBAL parse before the noun parse ('for swearing' briefly became bindharr'yunawuy+puy, a double suffix — caught by the suite)

New verbs: nyäl'yun tell-a-lie, märr-yuwalkthirri believe, märr-djulkthun disbelieve, bokman create (vocab), mata'marama tie up; C's -kuŋu possessor of these nouns (ŋarrakuŋu wukirriwuy) attested — the possessive machinery would give -kalaŋu forms; religious C items omitted per standing rule; mata'maranhawuy 'prisoner' vs mata'maranhamirri 'policeman' recorded (see Lesson 72 note)

lessons.title: Derived words (14-15): quaternary form as adjective and noun

rules.statement: A. The quaternary form with NO suffix behaves like an adjective or noun, same meaning as quaternary + -buy/-puy/-wuy. B. Adjective: yothu wir'yuna(ra) a thin child; yolŋu yal'yuna(ra) a placid person; wäŋa muryuna(ra) a hot place; walu gulŋiyinyara the setting sun; matha nyäl'yunara untrue words; walu djulkthunara past days. C. Noun: guyaŋanhara thoughts, märr-ŋamathinyara love, märr-yuwalkthinyara faith, giti-ḏaw'yunara writing(s), milkunhara revelation, märr-djulkthunara unbelief. D. The bare quaternary also describes the object in the act (cf. Lesson 69-E): Ŋarra nhäŋala miyalknha ŋupanara / marrtjinyara / waṉḏinyara; Yapay ŋäkula djamarrkuḻi'nha ḻiyamanara / ŋäthinyara.

notes: D composed as the standing '-ra' alternative on every Lesson 69 enActo render (Ŋarra nhäŋala miyalknha waṉḏinyara appears as the option 'forma cuaternaria sin sufijo'); the accion: nouns carry corta+ra as base alterna (C)

B's adjectives (wir'yun thin, yal'yun placid, muryun hot-place, gulŋiyirri set-of-sun, djulkthun pass) are verbs already in verbs.json — the bare-quaternary attributive frame ('a thin child' with no EN adjective cue) stays attested; giti-ḏaw'yun and milkuma (milkunhara revelation) recorded

lessons.title: Derived words (16-17): verb + -mirri = adjective and noun

rules.statement: A. Lesson 42: short quaternary + -mirri = adjective of one who DOES the action (gal'yunamirri yothu, a crawling baby). B. The same suffix also makes an adjective of POSSESSING a quality: märr-ŋamathinyamirri yolŋu (a loving person); dhiŋganhamirri rom (a way of life possessing death); walŋa-gurrupanamirri rom (life-giving way); galŋa-djulŋithinyamirri wäŋa (a happy place); ḏukmaranhamirri dhukarr (a healing path); galŋa-miḏikinyamirri wäŋa (place of misery); wukirrimirri buṉbu (house of writing, i.e. school); dharaŋanamirri dhäwu (an understandable story). C. The same words behave as NOUNS: märr-ŋamathinyamirri love, guwaḻ-ṉirr'maranhamirri temptation, galŋa-djulŋithinyamirri happiness. NOTE: -mirri nouns sometimes equal -wuy nouns (märr-ŋamathinyamirri = märr-ŋamathinyawuy love), sometimes differ sharply: mata'maranhamirri one who ties up (policeman) vs mata'maranhawuy one who is tied up (prisoner).

notes: Recorded as data, not newly composed: the Lesson 42 agentive -mirri machinery already produces the doer readings; the quality/abstract readings (dhiŋganhamirri rom, wukirrimirri buṉbu 'school', galŋa- compounds, ḏukmarama heal, galŋa-miḏikirri be miserable, guwaḻ-ṉirr'marama tempt) are attested with their glosses

The policeman/prisoner minimal pair (mata'maranhamirri/-hawuy) is the cleanest -mirri (agent) vs -wuy (patient) contrast in the book — kept as a note for the future multi-analysis of 'one who X' phrasings

lessons.title: (A) Derived words (18): verb + -miriw = adjective (B) Negative commands

rules.statement: A. Lesson 9: noun + -miriw = without (yothumiriw childless). B. On the short quaternary (Yirrkala long) it means 'not possessing the quality / not doing the action': guya ḻukanhamiriw (non-edible fish), yothu marrtjinyamiriw (a child not yet able to walk), yothu waŋanhamiriw (not yet able to talk), yolŋu buny'tjunamiriw (a person who doesn't smoke), yolŋu nyäl'yunamiriw (who doesn't lie), djamarrkuḻi' ḻupthunamiriw (unwashed children), walŋa dhä-dhawar'yunamiriw (endless life), bakmaranhamiriw (unbroken, unbreakable), rom dhiŋganhamiriw (a way of life without death), yolŋu monhamiriw (who doesn't forget). C. Quaternary + -miriw makes a NEGATIVE COMMAND: Waŋanhamiriw! (Stop talking! Don't talk!), Marrtjinyamiriw!, Buny'tjunamiriw!, Ŋorranhamiriw!, Dhurrparanhamiriw! (Stop treading on it), Nhänhamiriw!, Malthunamiriw!, Buḻ'yunamiriw!

notes: B partly composed: EN 'un-' + participle → carencia:<verbo> adjective with gup = short quaternary + miriw (unwashed → ḻupthunamiriw letter-exact, unbroken → bakthunamiriw — the book's bakmaranhamiriw uses the transitive bakmarama, attested); the not-able-to / doesn't-V phrasings (a child who can't walk yet) stay attested

C composed: FraseIR.prohibitivoMiriw — EN 'stop + gerund' → [Quaternary]miriw! with the Yirrkala long form and the classic yaka-imperative as options; and every plain negative imperative (don't smoke / no fumes) now offers the -miriw command as an alternative; ES 'deja de + infinitivo' is already taken by the ganarrthun 'stop it' verb (Ganarrthulu buny'tjunarawa!) — a legitimate composition, the -miriw reading noted
dhä-dhawar'yun (finish) and dhurrparan (tread) exist in verbs.json; malthun follow ✓; moma forget → monhamiriw attested via the B list

lessons.title: Verbs behaving as adverbs of manner

rules.statement: A. Beyond the pure manner adverbs (Lesson 12: bondi quickly, rrambaŋi together), verbs are very often used as adverbs of manner — and must AGREE IN FORM (tense etc.) with the verb they modify. B. roŋanmarama (back): Djuy'yurru roŋanmaraŋu! (Send it back — both secondary); Ŋarra gäŋala roŋanmaraŋala (I brought it back — both tertiary); Ŋayi dhu yaka rulwaŋdhun roŋanmarama (both primary). dhawar'marama (all up): Ŋayi ḻukana dhawar'maraŋala. yätjama (badly): Ŋayi gana bala' dhuḻ'yurruna yätjaŋala. nyilŋ'marama (down — religious example omitted by request). mukthun (quietly): Mukthurru nhini! ḻatjuwarr'marama (out): Barpuru ŋarra ḻatjuwarr'marama ŋatha gurrupan djamarrkuḻi'nha (as printed — user re-checked and kept verbatim; the form pairing is unusual). C. Adjective-derived verbs (Lessons 49-50) as manner adverbs: Ḏarrtjalkkuŋu guyaŋi! (Think cleanly); Dhäwu ŋayi ḻakaraŋala yuwalkkuŋala (told it truthfully); Barpuru ŋayi ga wukirri manymakkuma (wrote well); Manymakkuŋu ŋayathulu! (Hold it properly); Ŋayathulu dhunupayaŋu! (Hold it straight); Dhäwu ŋayi märraŋala dhaŋaŋguŋala (got the story fully). NOTES: a transitive verb takes a transitive adverb; an intransitive one sometimes either (Mukthurru nhini / Manymakkuŋu nhini; Ŋayi marrtjina ḻiw'yurrana~ḻiw'maraŋala he went around). D. Two verbs used together agree in form: Ŋayi waṉḏina yatjurruna / ŋäthina / gitkitthurruna / ḏar'ṯaryurruna / gukthurruna / murryurruna (He ran yelling / crying / laughing / singing / barking / growling). E. mirithirri and muŋbunuma are adverbs that cannot stand as verbs but have all four forms and agree: mirithirri (group 4): Ŋayi ga mirithirri ḏar'ṯaryun (singing loudly); Barpuru ŋayi ga djäma mirithirri (worked hard); Mirithirri ŋarra yurru waṉḏirri (I'll run fast); Mirithi dhä'yurru (open wide); Yaka buŋu mirithi (don't hit hard); Nyilŋ'thurru mirithi; Walala gana djaŋŋarrthina mirithina (very hungry); Mirithina ŋayi rurrguyurruna (scrubbed hard); Yothu gana ŋäthina mirithina; Yaka ŋarra mirithinya(ra) barrarinya(ra); Balaŋu nhe yaka ŋanya guyaŋanha(ra) mirithinya(ra); Ŋayi nhuŋu djäl ḏar'ṯaryunarawa mirithinyarawa. NOTE: qualifying an ADJECTIVE, mirithirri stays unchanged: Dhuwala guya yindi mirithirri (very big); Gäthura ŋarra nhäŋala mirithirri yindi guya. muŋbunuma (group 7, 'for good'): Ŋayi dhu marrtji muŋbunuma; Yaka marrtji muŋbunuŋu; Ŋayi marrtjina muŋbununala (printed — engine muŋbunuŋala per the verb table); Ŋayi djäl marrtjinyarawa muŋbununharawa. F. warrpam'/bukmak (all) verbalised as adverbs where English uses none: Nhe balaŋu moŋu warrpam'thurru (You might forget everything); Ŋayi dhu marŋgikuma nhumalanha warrpam'kuma; Nhe ga nhäma ŋanapurrunha bukmakkuma; Ŋayi djuy'yurruna walalanha warrpam'thurruna.

examples.en: He was building the house badly

lessons.title: Emphasised personal pronouns: -pi, -wuy, -giyin-/-kiyin-

rules.statement: A. The Lesson 5 pronouns — in verbless sentences (L1: Ŋarra manymak, I'm good), as subject of an intransitive verb (L24: Ŋanapurru marrtjina, We went), as agent of a transitive verb (L22: Maṉḏa nhäŋala, They saw) — are emphasised with the suffixes -pi and -wuy: Ŋarrapi yurru marrtji (I myself shall go), Nhepi yurru marrtji, Ŋayipi yurru marrtji, Ŋalipi yurru marrtji, Ŋalinyupi yurru marrtji, Nhumapi yurru marrtji, Maṉḏapi yurru marrtji. NOTE: the English could also be YOU (no-one else) will go, THEY (no-one else) will go. B. Object pronouns (L20) are emphasised: singular ŋarrapinya / nhunapinya / ŋanyapinya (Ŋayi dhu ŋarrapinya nhäma — He'll see ME, no-one else); dual and plural add -wuy- before the final -nha of the object form: ŋalitjalanhawuynha, ŋalinyalanhawuynha, nhumalanhawuynha, maṉḏanhawuynha, ŋalimurrunhawuynha, ŋanapurrunhawuynha, walalanhawuynha. NOTE: the singular alternates ŋarranhawuynha (me), nhunapinyawuy (you), ŋanyapinyawuy (her, him) are sometimes used instead. C. When a personal pronoun possessing suffix -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu is emphasised, -wuy is added: Ŋarrakuwuy ŋayi wäthurruna (She called ME, no-one else), Nhuŋuwuy, Nhanŋuwuy, Ŋalitjalaŋguwuy, Ŋalinyalaŋguwuy, Nhumalaŋguwuy, Maṉḏaŋguwuy, Ŋalimurruŋguwuy, Ŋanapurruŋguwuy, Walalaŋguwuy. D. When a personal pronoun possessing suffix -gala/-kala/-wala is emphasised, the infix -giyin-/-kiyin- is inserted: Ŋarrakiyingala ŋayi ḻakaraŋala (He told ME, no-one else), Nhokiyingala, Nhanukiyingala, Ŋalitjalaŋgiyingala, Ŋalinyalaŋgiyingala, Nhumalaŋgiyingala, Maṉḏaŋgiyingala, Ŋalimurruŋgiyingala, Ŋanapurruŋgiyingala, Walalaŋgiyingala. E. The infix -giyin-/-kiyin- is also inserted when emphasising the possessing suffix -guŋu/-kuŋu/-wuŋu (L30): Ŋarra nhokiyinguŋu märraŋala dhäwu (I got the story from YOU); and the possessing infix -galaŋu-/-kalaŋu-/-walaŋu- (L29, 39, 53): Nhanukiyingalaŋuŋuru ŋarra bilyurruna (I turned away from HER); Ŋarra maṉḏaŋgiyingalaŋuwuy dhäwu nhanukala ḻakaraŋala (I told her about THEM); Limurru dhu marrtji Nhanukiyingalaŋuwurru (We must go through HIM, no-one else). NOTES: 1. -kiyin- with singular personal pronouns (as it follows a vowel); -giyin- with dual and plural (as it follows a nasal). 2. After -kiyin-/-giyin- the infix -galaŋu- is used as it follows a nasal (never -kalaŋu- or -walaŋu-). 3. The same abbreviations and Yirrkala differences apply as for the unemphasised forms. 4. At Yirrkala -way is often used instead of -wuy: ŋanapurruŋguway.

examples.en: I got the story from YOU

notes: Mechanisms, all computed from the existing pronoun tables: (A) SujetoIR.enfatico — the wrapper strips 'PRON myself/yourself/himself/herself/ourselves/yourselves/themselves' (ES 'PRON mismo/misma/mismos/mismas') and the generator post-stage aplicarEnfasisSujeto appends -pi to the subject pronoun token in the main gup and every alternative, deriving the base-variant alternatives (ŋalinyupi, rrapi-type) from VOCAB.variantes per NOTE 3; (B) ObjetoIR.enfatico — 'only + object pronoun' (ES 'solo/solamente a mí...') renders formaObjetoEnfatico: the three singulars are the suppletive data table objetosEnfaticos (ŋarrapinya/nhunapinya/ŋanyapinya), non-singular = VOCAB.objetos + wuynha computed; the NOTE's singular alternates are offered as alternativas (1sg objeto+wuynha, 2sg/3sg main+wuy); (C) dative-object verbs with enfatico render enfatizarPosesivo = posesivo+wuy, with the Yirrkala -way substitution (note 4); (D) the tell/speak oblique variants render enfatizarComitativo — -kala → -kiyingala after vowels, -gala → -giyingala after nasals (note 1) — as options on the marcoContar/marcoHabla frames; (E) OrigenIR.enfatico ('from only you') feeds the SAME enfatizarComitativo through the existing origen machinery: formaGunu gives nhokiyinguŋu (E1) and the -ŋuŋuru chain gives nhanukiyingalaŋuŋuru (E2a) with no new render code

Word order: the book fronts the emphasised C/D forms (Ŋarrakuwuy ŋayi wäthurruna); the engine's main order keeps the frame order with the fronted form among the alternativas where the existing order-alternatives produce it — fronting as MAIN for emphatics recorded as pending

E2b (maṉḏaŋgiyingalaŋuwuy 'about THEM') and E2c (Nhanukiyingalaŋuwurru 'through HIM' perlative) attested — the galaŋu+wuy/wurru chains ride on pertenencia/perlativo paths not yet carrying enfatico; ES 'por'-emphatics and 'nosotros dos mismos' (dual) unexpressed in ES input

A-forms print yurru (the book's future particle); the engine's main uses dhu with yurru among the alternatives (lesson 7 variante), so the A examples verify as attested while the composition is asserted in the regression suite with real outputs

lessons.title: Emphasised possessive adjectives: -wuy; -giyin-/-kiyin-

rules.statement: A. To emphasise Possessive Adjectives (1) — see Lessons 13/35 — the suffix -wuy is added: Dhuwala ŋarrakuwuy yiki (This is MY knife, no-one else's); Maṉḏaŋguwuy yothu dhiŋgaŋala (THEIR baby died, no-one else's); Ŋarra nhäŋala nhanŋuwuy miyalknha (I saw HIS wife, no-one else's). B. To emphasise Possessive Adjectives (2) — see Lesson 36 — the infix -giyin-/-kiyin- is used (for full list see Lesson 75, Section D): Nhanukiyingala miyalkthu manaŋina (HIS OWN wife stole it); Gäŋu ŋarrakiyingala wäŋalili (Take it to MY place, no-one else's); Maṉḏa märraŋala nhokiyingala rrupiyay (They got it with YOUR money, not their own). C. To emphasise Possessive Adjectives (3) — see Lessons 51, 52 — the infix -giyin-/-kiyin- is inserted before the infix -galaŋu-/-kalaŋu-/-walaŋu-: Maṉḏaŋgiyingalaŋuwa djurra'wa ŋarra djälthina (I want THEIR books, no-one else's); Gurrupulu ŋarrakiyingalaŋuwala miyalkkala (Give it to MY wife, no-one else's); Napurru yurru nhokiyingalaŋuwurru dhuwurrkurru marrtji (We shall go along YOUR way, no-one else's). NOTES: 1. -kiyin- with singular possessive adjectives (my/your/his/her) as it follows a vowel (ŋarra-/nhe-/nhanu-); -giyin- with dual and plural as it follows a nasal. 2. After -kiyin- or -giyin- the infix -galaŋu- is used as it follows a nasal (never -kalaŋu- or -walaŋu-). 3. Possessive Adjectives made from nouns (for example Djäwa's, the baby's) do NOT take the suffix -wuy or the infix -giyin-/-kiyin-.

examples.en: They got it with YOUR money (not their own)

notes: Mechanism: posesivoEnfatico — separarPoseedorNP captures 'only + possessive determiner + N' (ES 'solo/solamente mi...') and camposPoseedor carries the flag into EVERY frame that already parses possessors (subject, object, verbless predicate, destination, instrument); the generator renders enfatizarPosesivo (posesivo+wuy, L75 helper) for -gu frames — fronted before the head noun in the verbless predicate (Dhuwala ŋarrakuwuy yiki) — and enfatizarComitativo (-kala→-kiyingala / -gala→-giyingala) inside renderPoseedorComitativo for the L36 oblique frames, which renderPoseedorInfijado then chains into the L51-53 -galaŋu- forms (ŋarrakiyingala+ŋu+wala/wurru) with no extra code
Note 3 is already respected structurally: noun possessors (posesivoNombre/posesivoSustantivo) never take the flag paths — only posesivo (pronoun determiners) do

C examples (djälthina want-frame with dative books, gurrupulu give + person allative chain) attested — those frames don't yet carry the flag; B ex.1 (ergative subject possessor nhanukiyingala miyalkthu) composes only if the suffixed-head subject path routes renderPoseedorComitativo

lessons.title: Reflexive possessive adjectives: -wuy; -giyin-/-kiyin-

rules.statement: A. 'They returned to their own country' — the possessing adjective refers to the same people as the Subject: it is REFLEXIVE; English often uses 'own'. B. Reflexive of Possessive Adjectives (1) — L35 — possessive + -wuy, optionally followed by the subject pronoun: Ŋarra dhu rupa gäma ŋarrakuwuy (ŋarra) — I shall bring my own pannikin; Nhe dhu rupa gäma nhuŋuwuy (nhe); Ŋayi dhu rupa gäma nhanŋuwuy (ŋayi); Ŋali... ŋalitjalaŋguwuy (ŋali); Ŋalinyu... ŋalinyalaŋguwuy (ŋalinyu); Nhuma... nhumalaŋguwuy (nhuma); Maṉḏa... maṉḏaŋguwuy (maṉḏa); Ŋalimurru... ŋalimurruŋguwuy (ŋalimurru); Ŋanapurru... ŋanapurruŋguwuy (ŋanapurru); Walala... walalaŋguwuy (walala). NOTE: ŋarrakuwuy ŋarra is sometimes abbreviated to ŋarraku rra. C. Reflexive of (2) — L36: Ŋarra roŋiyina ŋarrakiyingala (ŋarra) wäŋalili — I returned to my own country; Nhe roŋiyina nhokiyingala (nhe) wäŋalili; Ŋayi roŋiyina nhanukiyingala (ŋayi) wäŋalili; Ŋali roŋiyina litjalaŋgiyingala (ŋali) wäŋalili; Linyu roŋiyina napurruŋgiyingala (linyu) wäŋalili (confirmed as printed — the book itself pairs linyu with napurruŋgiyingala); Nhuma roŋiyina nhumalaŋgiyingala (nhuma) wäŋalili; Maṉḏa roŋiyina maṉḏaŋgiyingala (maṉḏa) wäŋalili; Limurru roŋiyina limurruŋgiyingala (limurru) wäŋalili; Napurru roŋiyina napurruŋgiyingala (napurru) wäŋalili; Walala roŋiyina walalaŋgiyingala (walala) wäŋalili. D. Reflexive of (3) — L51, 52, 53: Ŋarra dhu ŋarrakiyingalaŋuwurru (ŋarra) romgurru marrtji — I shall go along my way; Nhe dhu nhokiyingalaŋuwurru (nhe) romgurru marrtji; Ŋayi dhu nhanukiyingalaŋuwurru (ŋayi) romgurru marrtji; Ŋali dhu litjalaŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (ŋali) romgurru marrtji; Linyu dhu linyalaŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (linyu) romgurru marrtji; Nhuma dhu nhumalaŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (nhuma) romgurru marrtji; Maṉḏa dhu maṉḏaŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (maṉḏa) romgurru marrtji; Limurru dhu limurruŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (limurru) romgurru marrtji; Napurru dhu napurruŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (napurru) romgurru marrtji; Walala dhu walalaŋgiyingalaŋuwurru (walala) romgurru marrtji. NOTES: 1. The bracketed pronouns may be omitted if ambiguity is not likely to occur. 2. Some of the ŋa-/ŋi- prefixes have been omitted in this Lesson to save space — quite permissible in Gupapuyŋu. 3. Difference between emphasised and reflexive: a. Bäyay ŋatha märraŋala nhanŋuwuy (Djäwawa) — Bäya got HIS (Djäwa's) food (not yours or anyone else's); b. Bäyay ŋatha märraŋala nhanŋuwuy ŋayi — Bäya got his own food. 4. Sometimes the reflexive possessive adjective is used where in English we wouldn't use 'own': a. Napurru ŋuli dharrpan ŋanapurruŋguwuy napurru yätjkurru dhuwurr — We hide our sin; b. Ŋarra ŋäŋ'thurruna ŋanya ŋarrakiyingalaŋuwa djoŋgu'wa — I asked him for my hat (the possessive adjective is the same person as the Agent or Subject). 5. The Subject (or Agent) of a command is 'you' (understood): [religious example omitted by request — the reflexive is nhuŋuwuy nhe]. 6. Possessive Adjectives made from nouns (Djäwa's, Stephen's, the woman's, the children's) do not take the suffix -wuy or the infix -giyin-/-kiyin-.

examples.en: I shall bring my own pannikin
You shall bring your own pannikin
He shall bring his own pannikin
They shall bring their own pannikin
I returned to my own country
They returned to their own country

notes: Mechanism: posesivoReflexivo — separarPoseedorNP captures 'possessive determiner + own + N' (ES 'mi propio/propia...') in every possessor frame; -gu objects render posesivo+wuy MOVED to clause-final position by the generar() post-stage aplicarPosesivoReflexivo (Ŋarra dhu rupa gäma ŋarrakuwuy), with the explicit reflexive pronoun (…ŋarrakuwuy ŋarra, notes 1 and 3) and the 1sg abbreviation ŋarraku rra as alternativas; destination possessors render the L76 kiyin-form in place (roŋiyina ŋarrakiyingala wäŋalili) with the pronoun-apposition alternativa; a noun subject takes the 3sg pronoun ŋayi (note 3b)

Reflexivity is triggered ONLY by explicit 'own'/'propio' — auto-detecting possessor=subject (note 4) would silently change every existing possessive sentence, so note 4 is recorded as data, not automated

D (romgurru perlative chains) rides the renderPoseedorInfijado machinery when the perlative frame carries the flag — not yet wired, attested; C's 'Linyu roŋiyina napurruŋgiyingala' confirmed as printed by user; note 5's example omitted (religious), the mechanism (imperative subject = you-understood → nhuŋuwuy nhe) recorded
New vocab: rupa pannikin (banikin as base alterna; wordlist also gives danhaŋa)

lessons.title: Reflexive personal pronouns

rules.statement: A. 'I saw myself' — the object pronoun is the same person as the Subject (Gupapuyŋu: Agent), so it is REFLEXIVE. B. Reflexive personal pronouns taking suffix -nha are the Lesson 75-B emphatic object forms, optionally followed by the subject pronoun: Ŋarra nhäŋala ŋarrapinya (ŋarra) — I saw myself; Nhe nhäŋala nhunapinya (nhe); Ŋayi nhäŋala ŋanyapina (ŋayi) (confirmed as printed — single-n variant; L75 gives ŋanyapinya); Ŋali nhäŋala litjalanhawuynha (ŋali); Linyu nhäŋala linyalanhawuynha (linyu); Nhuma nhäŋala nhumalanhawuynha (nhuma); Maṉḏa nhäŋala maṉḏanhawuynha (maṉḏa); Limurru nhäŋala limurrunhawuynha (limurru); Napurru nhäŋala napurrunhawuynha (napurru); Walala nhäŋala walalanhawuynha (walala) — dual/plural mean '-selves' OR 'each other'. C. Reflexive pronouns taking -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu are the possessive+wuy forms: Ŋarra gana wuyurruna ŋarrakuwuy (ŋarra) — I was sorry for myself; Nhe... nhuŋuwuy (nhe); Ŋayi... nhanŋuwuy (ŋayi); ...litjalaŋguwuy / linyalaŋguwuy / nhumalaŋguwuy / maṉḏaŋguwuy / limurruŋguwuy / napurruŋguwuy / walalaŋguwuy. MORE EXAMPLES: Ŋarra maypal bumara ŋarrakuwuy ŋarra (I got some shellfish for myself); Ŋayi djäl guŋga'yunarawa nhanŋuwuy ŋayi (He wants to help himself); Nhe marŋgi ŋäminarawa nhuŋuwuy nhe (You know how to paint yourself); Djarrami ŋayi märraŋala nhänharawa nhanŋuwuy ŋayi (He got a mirror to look at himself). D. Reflexive pronouns taking -gala/-kala/-wala are the Lesson 75-D kiyin-forms: Ŋarra waŋana gana ŋarrakiyingala (ŋarra) — I was talking to myself; Nhe... nhokiyingala (nhe); Ŋayi... nhanukiyingala (ŋayi); ...litjalaŋgiyingala / linyalaŋgiyingala / nhumalaŋgiyingala / maṉḏaŋgiyingala / limurruŋgiyingala / napurruŋgiyingala / walalaŋgiyingala. NOTES: 1. ŋa-/ŋi- prefixes omitted in a number of cases (permissible). 2. Bracketed words may be omitted. 3. Dual and plural reflexive denote either '-selves' or 'each other'; if ambiguity is likely, use the construction of Lesson 79 note 4.

notes: Mechanism: ObjetoIR.reflexivo — EN self-words (myself/yourself/himself/herself/itself/ourselves/yourselves/themselves) and 'each other'/'one another' parse as objects carrying reflexivo+enfatico (the reflexive forms ARE the L75 emphatic forms); ES 'a sí mismo/a mí mismo/a ti mismo...' and 'el uno al otro'; a persona-less reciprocal is filled from the subject in analizar() (noun subjects default 3pl)

The accusative render therefore produces the B construction for free (Ŋarra nhäŋala ŋarrapinya); the trailing bracketed subject pronoun is an alternativa (nota 2); C (-guwuy dative frames, wuyun 'feel sorry for') and D (-kiyingala oblique frames) ride enfatizarPosesivo/enfatizarComitativo when the frame carries the object — D composes through the talk-to frame, C's wuyun verb not yet in vocab (attested)
New vocab: djarrami mirror; maypal shellfish already present (L21); 'Ŋayi nhäŋala ŋanyapina' as printed (single n) vs L75 ŋanyapinya — confirmed by user

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs: -mirri (group 9)

rules.statement: A. Verbs are made reflexive by adding -mirri to the SHORT QUATERNARY form (Yirrkala: long form) of all groups EXCEPT groups 5 and 6, where -mirri is added to the PRIMARY form. -mirri is not added to Group 1 verbs. All reflexive -mirri verbs form a new group (9): PRIMARY -mirri, SECONDARY -mirri, TERTIARY -mina, QUATERNARY -minya. Ŋarra ga waŋanhamirri (I am talking to myself); Ŋarra ga guyaŋanhamirri (thinking of myself); Ŋarra ga nhänhamirri (looking at myself); Ŋarra ga ḻawunhamirri (biting myself); Ŋayi yurru ḻakaranhamirri (She will tell on herself, confess); Ŋayi yurru dharpunhamirri (spear herself); Ŋayi yurru ŋurrkanhamirri (throw herself down); Ŋayi yurru bunhamirri (beat herself); Barpuru ŋarra wutthunmirri (Yesterday I hit myself); Barpuru ŋarra mitthunmirri (cut myself); Barpuru ŋarra yirrpanmirri (scratched myself); Barpuru ŋarra ŋäminmirri (painted myself); Walala gana waŋanhamina (They were talking to each other); Walala gana bunhamina (fighting, lit. beating each other); Walala gana dharrpanmina (hiding themselves); Walala gana galkunmina (having a rest, lit. waiting for themselves/each other); Balaŋu nhuma yaka nhänhaminya(ra) (You shouldn't have looked at each other); Balaŋu nhuma yaka waŋanhaminya(ra); Balaŋu nhuma yaka bunhaminya(ra) (You shouldn't have fought); Balaŋu nhuma yaka dharrpanminya(ra). B. Reflexive verbs can be used with or without reflexive pronouns: 'He cut himself' = Ŋayi mitthunmina / Ŋayi mitthunmina ŋayipi (L75-A) / Ŋayi mitthunmina ŋanyapinya ŋayi (78-B) / Ŋayi mitthurruna ŋanyapinya ŋayi. MORE EXAMPLES: Walŋakunhamirri nhunapinya/nhepi nhe (Save yourself); (two religious examples omitted by request); Maṉḏa ga djälthirri märranhaminyarawa maṉḏaŋguwuy maṉḏa (They want to get married, lit. to take each other; note -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu after djäl). NOTES: 1. All reflexive -mirri verbs are intransitive. 2. Some verbs are reflexive in themselves without -mirri: ḻupthun wash oneself. 3. Groups 5/6: guŋga'yunmirri = help oneself (primary + -mirri) vs guŋga'yunamirri = helper (quaternary + -mirri, Lesson 4). 4. Dual/plural = '-selves' or 'each other'; to disambiguate: a. Walala ga märr-ŋamathinyamirri walalaŋguwuy walala bala räli' yunmirri (They love each other — bala-räli 'backwards and forwards' verbalised reflexive to agree with 'love'); b. the nhakuna construction spelling out 'he loves himself, and he loves himself, and so on' (They love themselves).

examples.en: They were talking to each other

notes: Mechanism: generar() post-stage aplicarReflexivoVerbal (before subject emphasis, like aplicarManera) — for a declarative verbal clause whose object is reflexivo: formasReflexivas computes the group-9 verb from the paradigm tables (groups 5/6 → primary + mirri; other groups → short quaternary + mirri; group 1 → none), PREFERRING an attested verbs.json group-9 entry when one exists (bunhamirri, nhänhamirri, waŋanhamirri, galkunmirri, yirrpanmirri are already transcribed); identificarForma finds the main verb token's form I-IV in the finished gup and swaps in the reflexive form at the SAME form (I/II -mirri, III -mina, IV -minya), removing the reflexive-pronoun token — tense agreement (ga+I, barpuru+I, III past, balaŋu yaka IV) is inherited automatically

The four B constructions are the main + alternativas: main = reflexive verb (Ŋayi mitthunmina); alts = pronoun construction (Ŋayi mitthurruna ŋanyapinya), + subject pronoun (…ŋanyapinya ŋayi), reflexive verb + ŋayipi (L75-A), reflexive verb + ŋanyapinya ŋayi

Noun subjects keep the pronoun construction as main (the ergative would have to be stripped for the intransitive reflexive — pending); note 4's bala-räli' yunmirri disambiguation and the nhakuna construction attested; note 2 (ḻupthun inherently reflexive) already respected — 'wash yourself' frames never carried an object
Religious examples omitted by request (the [name]wala give/show sentences); 'Save yourself' kept as data, not asserted

lessons.title: Parts of the human body; parts of animals or inanimate objects

rules.statement: A. In English possessive adjectives go with body parts (my head, his foot); in Gupapuyŋu the body part on the body is regarded as ONE with the person (the possessive form is only sometimes used). B. As SUBJECT of an intransitive verb: Ŋarra ḻiya rathala'yurruna (My — lit. I — head is aching); Ŋarra diltji rirrikthurruna (My back is sore); Ŋarra goŋ bakthurruna (My hand is hurt, from bumping); Ŋarra djalkiri burakina (My foot is hurt, skin pierced); Ŋarra gulaŋ waṉḏina (My blood ran/flowed); Ŋarra goŋ gärrina bathilili (My hand entered the basket); Ŋarra maŋutji bambaythina (My eyes shut); Ŋarra ḻambarr yätjina (My shoulder has gone wrong). C. As OBJECT of a transitive verb: Ŋarra ŋanya dhakal bartjunmaraŋala (I slapped his — lit. him — face/cheek); Ŋarra ŋanya ḻiya wutthurruna (I hit his head); Ŋarra ŋanya wana ŋayathaŋala (I touched his arm); Ŋarra ŋanya marra mitthurruna (I cut his hair). D. With suffix -lili: Gärri ŋarrakala ḻiyalili (Come into my — lit. me — mind); Gärri ŋarrakala ŋayaŋulili (…my life); Gärri ŋarrakala ŋoylili/ḏoṯurrklili (…my heart). NOTE: ŋoy is the seat of emotion; the literal ḏoṯurrk 'heart' is widely accepted through mission use. E. WITH REFLEXIVE VERB (subject acts on part of own body): Ŋarra marra mitthunmina (I cut my — lit. myself — hair); Ŋarra ḻuku gänhamina dispensarylili (I took my foot to the dispensary); Ŋarra buthuru gunganhamina (I shut my ears, wouldn't listen); Ŋarra buthuru djaw'yunmina (I took my ears away); Ŋarra ḻiya wutthunmina (I hit my head); Ŋarra buku dharrpanmina (I hid my face). ANOTHER REFLEXIVE: Maṉḏa goŋ ŋayathanhamina (They held/shook hands). NOTES: 1. Reflexive pronouns can accompany the reflexive verb: Ŋarra marra mitthunmina ŋarrapinya ŋarra. 2. Words, name, subsection, photo are also one with the person: Yol nhe yäku? (What's your name? lit. Who you name?); Ŋarra ŋanya yäku ḻakaraŋala (I called his — lit. him — name); Nhä nhe mälk? (What is your subsection?); Bäpay maṉḏanha mali märraŋala (Bäpa took their — lit. them — photo); Bäpa matha djuy'yunmina djimiṉḏi'kurru (Bäpa sent word on the wireless). F. Parts of animals or inanimate objects are one with the whole — the suffix -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu is not generally used: weṯi yaŋara' (a wallaby's tail), garriwa mapu' (a turtle's egg), wäk bulpul (a crow's feather), menduŋ mäny (a snail's trail), guḻawurr binbarr (the wing of a jungle fowl), marra dharpa (the leaves of a tree), wana dharpa (the branch), makarr dharpa (the roots), buku dharpa (the tree top), maŋal' maŋutji (the hook of a spear thrower), ḻirra gara (the point of a spear), gurtha ṉilŋ'ṉilŋ' (the sparks of a fire), mitjiyaŋ ḏäthu' (a boat funnel).

notes: Mechanism: PalabraVocabulario.parteCuerpo (head, hair, arm, back, blood, cheek, shoulder, ear, eye, face, hand, foot, heart, life, name, subsection, photo, word, tail, feather, egg...) + SujetoIR/ObjetoIR.parteCuerpo. B: a 'my/his + body-part' SUBJECT of an intransitive VP becomes {persona, parteCuerpo} — rendered [pronoun][part][verb] with the possessive form as alternativa (lección 80-A 'sometimes used'). C: the same possessor+part OBJECT becomes {persona, parteCuerpo} — rendered [ŋanya-form][part bare][verb] with the nhanŋu possessive alternativa. E: when the possessor equals the subject the object auto-flags reflexivo and the L79 machinery produces the mirri-verb (Ŋarra marra mitthunmina) with note-1's ŋarrapinya ŋarra construction among the alternativas — ES 'corté mi pelo' symmetric. F: a non-person possessor of a parteCuerpo head juxtaposes [whole][part] with the -wa suffixed form as alternativa (Dhuwala miyapunu mapu'). Note 2's name-question composes as the dedicated yolyaku frame (what's your name / ¿cómo te llamas? / ¿cuál es tu nombre? → Yol nhe yäku?) and 'i said his name' rides the C frame (said added to the irregular-past table)

New vocab (L80): marra hair, waṉa arm (guplist form; book prints wana), diltji back (back-body), gulaŋ blood, dhakal cheek, ḻambarr shoulder, buthuru ear, buku face, yäku name, mälk subsection, mali photo/image, matha word/tongue, yaŋara' tail, bulpul feather, ŋoy heart (ḏoṯurrk base alterna), ŋayaŋu life; verb ache = rathala'yun (standalone lemma already in verbs.json); 'sore' wired to rirrikthun via the stative-participle table; existing goṉ hand kept as transcribed at L33 (book prints goŋ here — guplist gives goŋ, discrepancy flagged)

Attested/pending: B3/B4/B7/B8 (bakthun/burakirri/bambaythirri/yätjirri frames with is-hurt readings), 'my back is sore' (is+stative-participle inside the body-part subject VP), D (-lili mind/life/heart imperatives with ŋarrakala), note 2 d-e (mali/matha frames), ES 'me corté el pelo' (article body-part with reflexive clitic — 'corté mi pelo' composes), ES 'trabajo todos los días' dropped-subject

lessons.title: Derived words (19): adverbs of time

rules.statement: A. Pure adverbs of time: barpuru yesterday; gäthura today, just now; goḏarr' in the morning; dunburrku in the middle of the night, late at night; yalala later on (L12). B. SECONDARY form of verb as adverb of time: boŋgama/break (of day) → boŋguŋu at daybreak, tomorrow; buwal'yun → buwal'yurru. C. Suffix -dhu/-thu/-yu/-y added to noun and adjective: ḻiyay waluy / ḏämbuy waluy at mid day; guwaḻyu munhay at midnight; goṉdhu barawundhu at twilight; wumbirryu gapuy at full tide; raŋiy gapuy at low tide; dhiyaŋu (bala) waluy on this day, today; dhiyaŋu (bala) ŋaḻindiy in this month; dhiyaŋu (bala) waltjaṉdhu in this year; dhiyaŋu (bala) munhay tonight; ŋuruŋi (bala) waluy/ŋaḻindiy/waltjaṉdhu/munhay on that day/month/year/night; wiripuŋuy waluy the other day, some other time, next day; wiripuŋuy ŋaḻindiy the other/next/last month; wiripuŋuy munhay the other night. Season examples: Ŋarra dhu marrtji wiripuŋuy guṉmalyu (next Wet Season) / mayalŋay / miḏawarryu (beginning of Dry) / rarranhdharryu (end of Dry). NOTES: 1. bala can be omitted but is very common. 2. dhiyaŋu bala = now (lit. on this day, waluy understood). 3. dhiyaŋu bili = just now (Dhiyaŋu bili ŋayi marrtjina). 4. ŋuruŋi and wiripuŋuy can refer to past or future — context decides. D. The same suffix on the QUATERNARY form of a verb: djaḏaw'yunaray / boŋganharay at day-break, at dawn; ŋurrithinyaray at the coming in of the tide; raŋithinyaray at the going out; walu-gärrinyaray at sun-set; ŋaḻindi-gärrinyaray at moon-set; walu-walmanharay at sun-rise; ŋaḻindi-walmanharay at moon-rise; ḻäy-bilyunaray (waluy) at about 1 pm; waluy ŋurru-yirr'yunaray on the first day; waluy dhä-dhawar'yunaray on the last day; buŋgulyu ŋurru-yirr'yunaray/dhä-dhawar'yunaray at the beginning/end of the corroboree; ŋurru-bilyunaray gapuy / dhapa-gulkthunaray gapuy at the turn of the tide. NOTE, two expressions: walu-dhuḏi-nhirrpanminyaray at sun-set (sun-putting-its-bottom-down, a REFLEXIVE quaternary); walu-goŋ-djalkthunminyaray at sun-rise (sun-throwing-its-hands-out). E. Suffix -mirri + -y (-mirriy): yalalaŋumirriy later on; dhä-dhawar'yunamirriy (waluy) on the last day; ḻiya-mukthunamirriy (waluy) on the last day; Christmasmirriy (waluy) at Christmas time; buŋgulmirriy (waluy) at the time of the corroboree; dharratharramirriy in June, July etc. NOTES: 1. -mirri makes the noun/verb an adjective modifying walu; -y makes it an adverb of time. 2. 'one day' = waŋganymirri waluy. F. Suffixes -mandhirri and -watjthirri on nouns = 'every X'; these adverbs AGREE IN FORM with the verb (cf. L74), declined like group 4: munhamandhirri/munhawatjthirri every day; ŋaḻindimandhirri/ŋaḻindiwatjthirri every month; dhuŋgarramandhirri/dhuŋgarrawatjthirri every year. Ŋarra ŋuli ga djäma yäna munhamandhirri (I work every day); the every-year example shows quaternary agreement: marrtjinyara dhuŋgarrawatjthinyara ([destination omitted — religious context]). NOTE: bitjan bili (L89-D) also combines: Ŋarra ŋuli ga bitjan bili djäma yäna munhamandhirri. G. Two isolated derived adverbs: walupuy in the day time (belonging to the day); munhagu/munhawu at night time (Yirrkala sometimes munhaku).

examples.gup: Ŋarra ŋuli ga djäma yäna munhamandhirri

notes: Composed as data + mechanism: the pure adverbs (dunburrku added; barpuru/gäthura/goḏarr'/yalala already present) and a lexicalised set of the derived forms as adverbio entries — at dawn djaḏaw'yunaray (boŋganharay/boŋguŋu/buwal'yurru base alternas), at sunset walu-gärrinyaray, at sunrise walu-walmanharay, at midday ḻiyay waluy, at midnight guwaḻyu munhay, in the daytime walupuy, at night munhagu (munhawu/munhaku alternas) — each derivation recorded in the rule text; 'he will go at dawn' → Djaḏaw'yunaray ŋayi dhu marrtji, 'they work at night' → Munhagu walala ga djäma

C seasonal/demonstrative -dhu forms (dhiyaŋu bala waluy, wiripuŋuy guṉmalyu...), D tide/corroboree forms, E -mirriy forms: transcribed as data in the rule text, attested — the productive derivations (IV+ray, -mirriy) are candidates for synthesis when input phrasings for them appear

lessons.title: Behaviour of certain verbs (2)

rules.statement: A. buna (arrive at/come to — no movement usually implied): 1. -ŋura on the THING arrived at: Djäwa barpuru buna wäŋaŋura (arrived at camp yesterday); …dhakalŋura (the island); …dhiyala (here). 2. NO suffix on a place name: Gäthura ŋayi bunana Darwin / Yirrkala / Maniŋgirirri. 3. -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu on a PERSON: Bäya bunana Stephengu / Djäwawa / ŋarraku. NOTE: sometimes -gala/-kala/-wala on the person, but -gu is more usual. B. gora (be shy/ashamed): -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu on the person BEFORE WHOM: Ŋayi ga gora miyalkku / Bäpawa / limurruŋgu; -gala/-kala/-wala on the person ON ACCOUNT OF whom (L66-D): Ŋarra gana gorana yapawala / nhokala / maṉḏaŋgala. C. djuḻuḻ'yun hide (intr), waṉḏirri run, wothirri disappear: -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu often on the person FROM whom the subject hides/runs/disappears: Ŋayi djuḻuḻ'yurruna Djäwawa; Ŋayi waṉḏina Djäwawa; Ŋayi wothina Djäwawa (Djäwa lost sight of him). D. ŋal'yun climb: -lili on the thing climbed: Bäya ŋal'yurruna dharpalili / ḻoḻulili / bala'lili. E. djuḻuḻ'yun + -lili on the thing IN WHICH the subject hides: Lorru ŋarraku djuḻuḻ'yurruna mulmulili / dharpalili / bathilili (hid from me in the grass / behind a tree / in a box). F. nhäma see, guŋga'yun help, guyaŋa think: -nha on the object and -lili on the place where the object is: Ŋarra ga nhuna guyaŋa dhipali (I am thinking of you there) / dhipali Darwinlili / dhipali Galiwin'kulili. NOTE: dhipali is used even when the place can't be seen nor is close. (Help-us examples: religious, omitted by request — the frame is [verb] [object-nha] dhipala [place-lili].) Ŋayi nhäŋala walalanha dhurrwaralili (saw them at the door) / dhawaḏalili (on the beach) / bala'lili (by the hut). NOTE, compare L69/71: Ŋayi ŋarranha nhäŋala giritjinyalili / marrtjinyalili / buḻ'yunalili (He saw me dancing / walking / playing — quaternary + -lili). G. nhäma: sometimes -lili to the thing and -gala/-kala/-wala to the person looked at: Nhäŋu dhipala (Look here); Nhäŋu dharpalili (Look at the tree); Nhäŋu ŋarrakala (Look at me). H. gulŋiyirri/gärri (enter, be inside): 'enter' → -lili: Djamarrkuḻi' bala'lili gulŋiyina/gärrina; storelili; dhipala. 'be inside' → -ŋura: Djamarrkuḻi' bala'ŋura gulŋiyirri/gärri ga; storeŋura; schoolŋura. I. bunhamirri fight (reflexive, L79): -ŋuru on the THING and -ŋuru or -gala/-kala/-wala on the PERSON fought over: Nhäŋuru maṉḏa ga bunhamirri? (What are they fighting over?) — Ŋathaŋuru / Ŋarali'ŋuru / Miyalkŋuru(-kala); Yolkala maṉḏa ga bunhamirri? (Whom…?) — Lorruwala / Balimaŋgala / Garmburrgala(-wala). J. ḏaḏawmarama stop, prevent: -ŋuru on the action prevented: Bäpay ŋanya ḏaḏawmaraŋala marrtjinyaŋuru (stopped him from going) / bindharr'yunaŋuru (swearing) / ŋathaŋuru ḻukanhaŋuru (eating the food) / ŋarali'ŋuru buny'tjunaŋuru (smoking the tobacco). NOTE: -ŋuru goes on the SHORT quaternary except at Yirrkala. K. ḏaḏawyun cease, dhawar'yun finish (intr): -ŋuru on the action ceased/finished: Rayman ḏaḏawyurruna buḻ'yunaŋuru / djämaŋuru / waŋanhaŋuru; Rayman dhawar'yurruna giritjinyaŋuru / ŋathaŋuru ḻukanhaŋuru / wukirriŋuru. NOTE: dhawar'yun intr (Rayman dhawar'yurruna ŋathaŋuru — finished eating) vs dhawar'marama trans (Raymandhu dhawar'maraŋala ŋatha — ate it all up). L. dhägir'yun forbid, punish: -ŋuru on the thing forbidden: Bäpay ŋanya dhägir'yurruna djämaŋuru / ŋarali'ŋuru / dhipuŋuru wäŋaŋuru (sent him off). NOTE: could read 'punished him by forbidding him work'. M. bilina finish/stop/cease (intr, IRREGULAR: its form never changes, no quaternary, takes no suffixes): as command: Bilina ŋarranha warku'yurru (Stop annoying me); Bilina ŋarranha ŋarrtjurru (Stop telling me off); Bilina ŋarranha nhäŋu (Stop looking at me); Bilina ŋarranha ŋayathulu (Stop touching me); as past: Bilina ŋayi dhipuŋuruyi wäŋaŋuru (He has finished with this place); Bilina nhuŋu dhäwu ŋarrakuŋu (That's all I have to say to you); Bilina mari (The trouble has finished). NOTE: bilin is the Dhuwal'mirr (Djambarrpuyŋu) form. N. gombuma take away from, got from: -nha on the person from whom taken: Bäpay yiki gombuŋala Djäwanha; Maṉḏa ŋarranha miyalk gombuŋala; Ŋatha gombuŋu dhuwali yothunha (Take the food away from that child). O. guwatjman come to a person (arriving at a person): -nha on the person arrived at: Djäway gäthura ŋarranha guwatjmara (Djäwa came to me today); Ŋarra dhu yalala Bäpanha guwatjman (I'll go to Bäpa later); Goḏarr' ŋarranha guwatjmulu (Come to me tomorrow). NOTE: in guwatjman do not release the tj sound.

notes: Grammar-as-data mechanisms: per-verb case-frame flags on VerboVocabulario. llegada (buna/arrive): renderDestino gives person → -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu (with the NOTE's -gala alternativa), non-proper thing → -ŋura, place name → bare (Barpuru ŋayi buna wäŋaŋura; Gäthura ŋayi bunana Darwin; Bäya bunana Stephengu all letter-exact from 'llegó a' / 'arrived at/in'). origenGu (waṉḏirri, wothirri, djuḻuḻ'yun): renderOrigen gives the from-person as -gu/-ku/-wa/-wu instead of -guŋu/-ŋuru (Ŋayi waṉḏina Djäwawa, Ŋayi wothina Djäwawa letter-exact); thing-origins unchanged. lugarLili (djuḻuḻ'yun): the place renders -lili instead of -ŋura (ES 'se escondió en la caja' → Ŋayi djuḻuḻ'yurruna bathilili = E3). subida (ŋal'yun/climb): the analyzer moves the thing-object to destino, rendering standard -lili (Bäya ŋal'yurruna dharpalili/ḻoḻulili letter-exact). K composes via FraseIR.accionNuru/objetoNuru: 'stopped/ceased/finished + gerund' (ES 'dejó/terminó/acabó de + inf' with pronoun subjects) → cease=ḏaḏawyun / finish=dhawar'yun + the action's SHORT quaternary + -ŋuru appended by the generar() post-stage aplicarAccionNuru, object nouns taking -ŋuru too (Rayman dhawar'yurruna ŋathaŋuru ḻukanhaŋuru letter-exact) and the Yirrkala long-quaternary alternativa per the J note. O composes as a plain transitive: visit = guwatjman (Gäthura Djäway ŋarranha guwatjmara — the -nha person IS the object)

Attested/pending: B gora 'in front of' -gu frame (the because-of -wala side already composes from L66), E full 'hid from me in the grass' (origen-gu + lili together), F dhipali/dhipala place-of-object frames and the quaternary+lili 'saw me dancing' variant (enActo currently renders -wuy per L69), G imperative nhäŋu frames, H 'be inside' -ŋura with ga, I fighting-over question/answer frames, J ḏaḏawmarama prevent-frame (needs object+action together), L dhägir'yun -ŋuru on plain nouns, M bilina irregular (warku'yun/ŋarrtjun verbs not yet in vocab), N gombuma -nha source frames, ES 'rayman dejó de jugar' with NAME subject (the name+preterite+purpose path intercepts; pronoun subjects compose)

lessons.title: Formation of plurals

rules.statement: Many devices form plural nouns, verbs and adjectives. A. Words plural in themselves (never singular): PLURAL ADJECTIVES djamandjaman/djamaparran/nyumurrku/yumurrku/djamawurru = little (sg yutjuwala, nyumukuṉiny); ḏilkurru/ḏilak = big (sg yindi, ḏumurru, bathala). NOTE: adjectives sometimes used as nouns (yumurrku = little ones, youngsters). PLURAL NOUNS djamarrkuḻi' children (sg yothu); yawirriny' initiated boys, ḏirrathala single boys/young men (sg gurrmul); manaŋa-ḏilkurru thieves (sg manaŋa-ḏumurru). NOTES: 1. dual = singular + maṉḏa (yothu / yothu maṉḏa / djamarrkuḻi'). 2. a plural adjective cannot be singular: WRONG Dhuwala yiki ḏilkurru. 3. a singular adjective is pluralised with mala: yindi mala djamarrkuḻi' (big children). PLURAL VERBS barrtjun spear (sg dharpuma); djalkthun throw (sg ŋurrkama); wäŋgama/garrarrakthun go, come, walk (sg marrtji); ḏäpthun sit (sg nhina); ḏurryun rise (sg rur'yun); gundupuma run (sg waṉḏirri); birrwirryun fly (sg butthun); djabarryun arrive (sg buna). NOTES: 1. plural verbs used when a. subject/agent is plural (Djamarrkuḻi wäŋgaŋala gana wäŋalili), b. object is plural (Ŋarra gana guya barrtjurruna dharrwa — I speared a lot of fish), c. action is plural (Dharrwamirri ŋanya barrtjurruna ŋuruŋi yolŋuy — speared him lots of times). 2. mass objects (water, sand) often take a plural verb: Gapu djalkthurru (Throw the water out). 3. singular verbs can be used instead: Djamarrkuḻi' marrtjina gana wäŋalili. 4. plural words never in a singular sense. B. DUPLICATION of whole or part: adjectives djawu'tjawuḻpa old (sg djawuḻpa), worru'worruŋu old (sg worruŋu), gurri'kurriri short (sg gurriri), yuḏayuḏa new/young (sg yuṯa — sounds change), wiripu wiripu other (two words, both take suffixes: wiripuŋulili wiripuŋulili wäŋalili malaŋulili); nouns yolŋu'yolŋu people, moṉu'moṉuŋu murderers, djika'tjikarr pimples, gaḏagaḏak uncircumcised boys (sg gaḏaku), gurrmu'kurrmul circumcised boys (sg gurrmul), wirrku'wirrkuḻ unmarried girls (sg wirrkuḻ); verbs nhina'nhina sit, ḻawu'ḻawuma bite, guya'kuyaŋa think, rulwa'rulwaṉdhun put, roŋi'roŋiyirri return, dhawadhawaṯthun/dhawayawaṯthun come out, mitmitthun cut, wutthuwutthun knock/hit many times. NOTE: duplication is not always plural (nyuŋunyuŋu wasp, barkparkthun sing vs barkthun pound). C. A quantity adjective with a singular noun forms the plural: dharrwa miyalk, ḻurrkun' yothu, warrpam' yolŋu; plural nouns also combine (bukmak djamarrkuḻi', dharrwa moṉu'moṉuŋu). D. walala and maṉḏa with a singular noun denote plural/dual for PEOPLE: Ŋunhi miyalk maṉḏa roŋiyina wäŋalili (The two women returned); (second example religious, omitted — the frame is noun + walala with matching case suffix). E. mala (plural) and maṉḏa (dual) with singular nouns/adjectives, people or things. MALA: no suffix → bare mala (Ŋarrakuwuy dhuwala djurra' mala — Those books are MINE); with -dhu/-thu/-yu/-y → malaŋuy (religious example omitted); with -wa → malaŋuwa (Ŋarra djäl dhiyaku yikiwa malaŋuwa — I want those knives); with -lili → malaŋulili (Ŋayi marrtjina wäŋalili wäŋalili malaŋulili — country after country, note the repetition). NOTES: 1. mala-plural takes infix -ŋu before a suffix; 2. mala = 'people, tribe, clan' takes NO infix (Ŋarra djäl ŋarrakiyingalaŋuwa malawa — I want my own people; Gupapuyŋuthu malay ŋarranha mundhurr gurrupara). MAṈḎA for two PEOPLE takes the pronoun maṉḏa's suffixes (Gurrupulu dhiyakala miyalkkala maṉḏaŋgala; Barpuru ŋarra nhäma ŋunhi ḏirramunha maṉḏanha; Gäthura ŋanya bumara ŋuruŋi maṉḏa yolŋuy); for two THINGS the noun's own suffix + infix -ŋu- (Rulwaṉdhurru dhipala ŋunhi yiki(nha) maṉḏaŋunha; Ŋarra djäl dhiyaku yikiwa maṉḏaŋuwa; Ŋayi ŋanya bumara dhiyaŋu yikiy maṉḏaŋuy; Ḏelili mala ŋal'yurruna waṉalili maṉḏaŋulili — the peewees hopped onto the wings; Djanda waṉḏina gana waṉakurru maṉḏaŋuwurru). NOTES: 1. two things as subject of intransitive/verbless: maṉḏany(nha) (Yiki maṉḏany(nha) ga ŋorra tableŋura); 2. as object -nha is usually added even with no noun suffix; 3. -ŋu- can be omitted before -nha. F. Suffix -wurru: ḏirramuwurru men, wiripuwurru others, dhuwalawurru these, ŋunhiwurru those; also on inherently plural words (dharrwawurru lots, ḏilkurruwurru elders); a final stop inserts -urru- (miyalkurruwurru women). Examples: Manymak miyalkurruwurruŋgu nhänharawa; Dhuwalawurru yolŋu mala barpuru marrtji dhakallili; Ḏirramuwurruy ŋatha manaŋina; Wiripuwurruŋgala gurrupulu; Barpuru ŋarra nhäma miyalkurruwurrunha. Plural 'these/those': -wurru on the L54/56 case forms + suffix (dhiyakuwurruŋgu — Ŋarra gana ḻarruŋala dhiyakuwurruŋgu djamarrkuḻi'wa; ŋuriŋiwurru — Ŋuriŋiwurruy yolŋuy malaŋuy guŋga'yurruna gana Bäpanha). NOTE: syllables run together (dhiyakuwurruŋgu → dhiyakurruŋgu; ŋurikiwurruŋgala → ŋurikurruŋgala) or an extra syllable appears (dhiyakurruwurruŋgu).

lessons.title: Suffixes -na, -dja/-tja/-nydja/-ny'tja, -nha, -dhi/-yi

rules.statement: A. SUFFIX -na: its use is not yet fully clear; it attaches to most word types in many positions, does not change meaning, and is a matter of style (not indiscriminate). In all previous Lessons -na was omitted to avoid confusion (except L61); in future Lessons it will be included. Do not confuse with: -nha object; -nha (84-C); -na tertiary (waŋana); -na short quaternary (bathana); -nha short quaternary (waŋanha). B. SUFFIX -dja/-tja/-nydja/-ny'tja: like -na (slight emphasis, mostly style). FORM RULES: 1. -dja after nasals m/n/ṉ/ny/ŋ (Balimaṉdja, waŋganydja, bathandja); 2. -tja after stops p/t/ṯ/tj/k and nasal+glottal m'/n'/ṉ'/ny'/ŋ' (miyalktja, ḻurrkun'tja); 3. -nydja after vowels, liquids l/ḻ/r/rr, y and w (ŋayinydja, nhenydja, dhakalnydja, manikaynydja); 4. after a glottal stop (except nasal+glottal) -ny- is inserted BEFORE the glottal and the rest becomes -tja (maŋalny'tja spear thrower, rakiny'tja rope, warrawny'tja shade). C. SUFFIX -nha: the object marker (L19/20: Ŋarra nhäŋala miyalknha) but also a -na-like stylistic use, often on adjectives in verbless sentences: Dhuwala djetji baḏarraŋnha (This sore is better). D. SUFFIX -dhi/-yi: EMPHASIS — 'too', 'as well', 'again'. Following nasals and stops → -dhi; following anything else, either form. Dhuwalayi/Dhuwaladhi yothu rirrikthun ga (THIS child is sick); Wanha Djäwa? Ŋunhayi/Ŋunhadhi nhina ga (Sitting over THERE); Dhiyaŋuyi/Dhiyaŋudhi ŋayi bumara ŋanya (He hit her with THIS); Maṉḏa buluyi/buludhi roŋiyina (They came back AGAIN); Bäpa yurru marrtji ga ŋarra yurru marrtjiyi/marrtjidhi (Bäpa is going and I'm going too); Gäthura goḏarr' ŋayi Ḏalmanalili marrtjina ga yalalaŋumirriy maku yurru roŋiyirriyi/roŋiyirridhi (…maybe will come back again later); A. Dhuwalanydja warraga. B. Ga nhä dhuwalanydja? A. Ŋunhanydja warragayi/warragadhi (That's a cycad too). NOTES: 1. -dhi contrasts with -thi (secondary of -thirri, L49): Walala balaŋu bäythi ŋathawa (They might miss out on their food); Bäydhi = Never mind. 2. -dhi is not used at Yirrkala — only -yi.
